raw:
These hypotheses come from comparing the 100 experiments within each edit type; most rest on a handful of comparisons, so treat them as moderately confident. The 10th is the weakest, since it rests on a single parent (experiment 39).

1. Edge 3 → nor_conv_1x1 gains more when edge 3 was `none`. Parents with edge 3 = none (92, 96–100) all gained, up to +14.8 to +24.4 on ImageNet16-120. Parents with a real op on edge 3 (91, 95) gained roughly nothing.
2. Edge 4 → skip_connect gains more when edge 3 is `none`. Experiment 72 gave +17.4 on ImageNet16-120, while the other parents sat near 0.
3. Edge 2 → none is worse when edge 2 is nor_conv_3x3. Experiments 43–45, 47 and 48 all lost accuracy on every dataset, while experiments 41 and 42 were about 0.
4. Edge 0 → nor_conv_3x3 gains less when edge 0 is avg_pool_3x3. Experiment 4 gave +3.7 on ImageNet16-120, against about +8.5 to +10 for other parents.
5. Edge 5 → nor_conv_3x3 gains less when edge 5 was `none`. Experiment 19 gave +2.6 on CIFAR-10, against +45 to +51 for skip_connect and avg_pool_3x3 on edge 5.
6. Edge 5 → nor_conv_3x3 gains more when edge 3 is `none`. Experiment 17 gave +20.6, +26.8 and +21.2, well above the other skip-based parents.
7. Edge 2 → nor_conv_3x3 gains less when edge 0 is `none`. Experiment 66 gave +0.8, +0.7 and +0.1, against +2 to +8 elsewhere.
8. Edge 2 → nor_conv_3x3 gains less when edge 5 is `none`. Experiment 69 gave +0.06, +1.28 and −2.07, below the other parents.
9. Edge 3 → nor_conv_1x1 gains more when edge 0 is `none`. Experiment 98 gave about +22 on all three datasets, against 1 to 3 points on CIFAR for the otherwise similar experiment 92.
10. Edge 4 → nor_conv_1x1 gains more when edge 5 is `none`. Experiment 39 was positive on all three datasets, while most other parents were near 0 or negative.
